newsitem.title: USA: White House's Stiglitz sees stable U.S. inflation.
newsitem.headline: White House's Stiglitz sees stable U.S. inflation.

text.p: White House economic adviser Joseph Stiglitz said Wednesday that U.S. inflation was stable and that the increase in consumer price inflation in September was due largely to special factors.

"The numbers today clearly indicate that the economy's inflation is at a very stable level," Stiglitz said in a speech to the National Economists Club. He said the increase to 0.3 percent in September from 0.1 percent in August was "almost completely anticipated." The increase was due to unexpected changes in apparel prices, new car price increases and the imposition of the airline ticket tax.
"We don't see any evidence of an increase in the overall rate of inflation going forward," Stiglitz added.

He noted that U.S. real wages are rising, but said wages were not "going up so fast as to be a threat in any way to inflation." Productivity is improving at a rate that allows more room for pay increases before wages become a threat to inflation, he said.
Stiglitz brushed aside any concerns over the outlook for consumer spending. He cited higher wages, rising consumer confidence, and improved net worths because of a robust stock market.
All of those factors "bode well for overall consumer spending," he told reporters after the speech.
